name: Conrad Davies
why: News frame from the Herald front-page package on the campus evangelist; his face fills the right of the frame, lit and looking almost into the lens, and it is the only photograph of him in the digitised run.

id_basis: The caption names two men in the frame, Davies and the visiting preacher Jim Gilles. The story inside the same issue describes Gilles standing on a manhole cover in a white shirt and black suspenders waving his Bible, and the man at the left edge of the frame is in a white shirt with a dark suspender strap, mouth open, an open book held below him. That fixes Gilles as the left figure and leaves the young man on the right, the one the crowd is watching, as Davies. He is a sophomore in April 2000, which makes him a freshman in 1998-99, the year the archive records him sworn in as an At-Large member.

name: Michael Hardin
why: The only labelled photograph of him in the digitised run, a People Poll head shot. The brim of his cap blacks out his eyes in the printed halftone, so the nose, mouth and jaw read but the upper face does not; offered because nothing else of him survives, and easy for an editor to drop.
id_basis: A five-across People Poll on the University Boulevard crosswalks. Each quote and name block is centred under its own head shot: the five photo blocks centre on x=117, 250, 383, 513 and 643 at 150 dpi and the first three name blocks on x=118, 252 and 385, so the first face carries the Hardin label. The printed name reads Michael Hardin at full scan resolution although the OCR makes it Herdin, and he is the only Michael Hardin in the digitised run. A Burkesville freshman in January 1997 is a sophomore in 1997-98, the year the archive seats him.

name: Troy Ransdell
why: His own columnist head shot, run beside the commentary he wrote against plus/minus grading; front-on, well lit and the best frame of him in the digitised run.
caption_quote: Troy Ransdell is a senior political science major from Louisville.
id_basis: A single-subject commentary mugshot with the name Troy Ransdell set in italic directly beneath the frame and the standing line at the foot of the column naming him again as the author, a senior political science major from Louisville. Nobody else appears in the frame. The tie to the office is contemporaneous and not merely nominal: the Herald of 9 March 2004, two days earlier, calls him SGA chief justice while reporting the constitutional referendum (digitalcommons.wku.edu/dlsc_ua_records/9381), and the Herald of 13 November 2001 had already introduced him as Louisville sophomore Troy Ransdell of SGA's Progressive Caucus.

name: Terry Woodall
why: A studio portrait in coat and tie, front-on and smiling, run in the Herald advertisement congratulating him as a Spirit Master; much the best frame of him in the digitised run.
id_basis: A two-portrait advertisement in which each photograph carries its own name in large small caps directly beneath it, TERRY WOODALL under the left frame and NATALIE CRONEY under the right, so this is a labelled single portrait rather than a grid keyed to a list. Two caveats for the editor. The tie to the Judicial Council justice of 2004-05 is the full name plus the cohort: the advertisement is about Spirit Masters and says nothing of student government, and no Herald story in the digitised run ties a Terry Woodall to SGA. Nothing else of him survives, and Woodall is uncommon at Western in these years - the only other trace is the 2003 Talisman, which lists Terry Woodall of Phi Delta Theta in the Greek Hall of Fame. Second, a Herald news photograph of 11 November 2004 (record 9420, front page) also names a Terry Woodall, identified by elimination from a caption that marks the other two men centre and right, but that man wears glasses and a beard and this one does not, so only this labelled portrait is offered.

id_basis: A five-across People Poll on whether classes should meet on Fridays. Each quote and name block is centred under its own head shot: the five photo blocks centre on x=173, 279, 385, 490 and 594 at 150 dpi and the name blocks on x=178, 284, 388, 493 and 600, a constant offset of about five pixels, so the first face carries the Beasley label. The Herald spells the surname Beasley where the archive has Beasly; the given name Arcentra is unique in the digitised run.

name: Amy Duncan
why: People Poll head shot, front-on and smiling; the only photograph of her in the digitised run.

Each name block is centred under its own head shot: the photo blocks centre on x=153, 266, 359, 461 and 566 at 150 dpi and the two name blocks the OCR recovered on x=357 and x=563, matching the third and fifth frames, so the third face carries the Duncan label. name: Kathleen Speicher
why: Herald opinion-page poll mugshot, front-on and clearly lit; the only usable photograph of her in the digitised run.
id_basis: The Herald's People Poll layout, running here under the question headline 'What do you think of Banshee?' rather than the poll's own name. Five framed head shots in a row across the foot of the Opinion page, each with its quotation and then its subject's name in bold and home town and class directly beneath its own frame. The five labels track the five frames left to right and each label centre sits within 0.013 of its frame centre: Adam Sharp 0.131 against frame 0.119, Amber Jackson 0.230 against 0.224, Derrick Herron 0.334 against 0.325, Angela Dennis 0.431 against 0.427, Kathleen Speicher 0.535 against 0.531. The fifth and rightmost face therefore carries the Speicher label. The cohort is confirmed twice over: this poll calls her a Louisville freshman in April 1999, and Shawn Poynter's bonfire picture of 10 November 1998 calls her one of two 'Louisville freshmen', which fits the Congress seat she was sworn into on 8 September 1998.

name: Jeff Swaim
why: Herald opinion-page poll mugshot, front-on and smiling; the only photograph of him in the digitised run. The halftone is crushed dark but the face reads.

name: Dana Lockhart
why: A studio head shot printed with his name set in bold directly beneath it, on the Herald's SGA candidate profile page. The sharpest photograph found for anyone on this block.
id_basis: An election-season candidate profile, 'Lockhart wants comfortable atmosphere', on a page headed 'SGA Candidates'. The nameplate 'Dana Lockhart' is centred at x=0.610 of the page width and the frame above it measures x 0.564 to 0.654, centre 0.609, so the label belongs to that frame and no other; the only other head shot on the page sits above the 'Patti Johnson' plate in the story beside it. The story identifies him at length as an SGA man: a junior from Hendersonville, Tenn., in his fifth semester in SGA, a member of Congress for three semesters, then a judicial council justice and at the time of writing SGA Parliamentarian, standing for executive vice president alongside presidential candidate Jessica Martin. name: Shavonna Smith
why: Cropped from the Herald's front-page photograph of 17 October 2002. The face is soft and turned down but the features read.
caption_quote: Graduate student Shavonna Smith talks with Bowling Green junior Nathan Bolton as they wait in line.
id_basis: The caption names exactly two people and the frame holds exactly two: a young man in a powered wheelchair and a standing woman. The man is Nathan Bolton, which the feature the picture illustrates establishes beyond doubt - 'Disabled students welcome helping hand' is written around Bolton, a Bowling Green junior with Transverse Myelitis who uses a wheelchair, and the second photograph on the same page is captioned 'Bolton, center, shares a laugh with friends during lunch'. The standing woman is therefore Shavonna Smith. Caveat for the editor: what is proved is that this face is the Shavonna Smith of October 2002. The tie to the Congress member of 1997-98 is the name plus the cohort - a graduate student in autumn 2002 fits an undergraduate career beginning about 1996 - and Shavonna is a rare enough first name that this is the only bearer of it anywhere in the digitised Herald 1993-2005.

A stage light has blown the highlights of her face to white and her eyes are shut in the moment of the hug, so hair, tiara, smile, jaw and earring read but the eyes do not. name: Mark Page
identification: FACE PROVED, PERSON NOT PROVED - FOR THE EDITOR
why: THE FRAME IS CERTAIN. College Heights Herald People Poll, 6 November 2001, printed p. 4: five students across the foot of the Opinion page, each head shot with its quotation beneath and then the name in bold with home town and class. His frame runs x 0.214 to 0.286 of the page width and the name line sits at x 0.208 directly under it; the next frame to the left is at x 0.100 to 0.171, one frame to each name, so the pairing cannot slide. The page is scanned 2,540 pixels wide, so the crop is 184 by 257. Soft and low in contrast, a snapshot in a baseball cap rather than a studio frame, but the face reads.
id_note: WHY THE PERSON IS FLAGGED, and it is a dating problem rather than a name problem. The archive's Mark Page is a rank-and-file Congress member of 1998-99, recorded absent from the roll calls of 8 and 15 September 1998. The man in this photograph is named in the Herald three other times and the sequence does not fit: on 29 August 2000 he is 'Louisville sophomore Mark Anthony Page', a bartender at a nightclub; on 6 November 2001 the poll calls him a Louisville senior; and on 2 May 2002 he is in the graduation list as Mark Anthony Page. A sophomore in autumn 2000 started at Western in 1999 at the earliest, which is a year after the Congress member is recorded in the minutes. He may be the same man advancing by credit hours rather than by year, and Louisville fits, but nothing in any source puts the man in this frame in student government. Not published on that basis.

why: THE FRAME IS CERTAIN. College Heights Herald People Poll, 9 November 1995, printed p. 4. This issue sets the poll as a vertical column down the right edge of the Opinion page rather than five across the foot: one head shot, then the quotation, then the name in bold with home town and class, repeated down the page. His frame runs x 0.843 to 0.926 of the page width with the name line at x 0.824 directly beneath it, and the frame above belongs to Joey Baldwin, Carrollton freshman, whose own label sits between the two. Front on, in focus, small only because the page is scanned 1,007 pixels wide.
id_note: WHY THE PERSON IS FLAGGED. This is the ONLY occurrence of the name Bill Brown in the digitised Herald of 1993-2005, and the dates work: a freshman in November 1995 is a senior in 1998-99, which is when SGA's minutes have Bill Brown on the floor speaking against the Kappa Alpha Order funding bill on 1 December 1998. But Bill Brown is one of the commonest names there is, the poll says nothing about student government, and the paper's silence on any other Bill Brown proves little for a name like this one. The photograph is of a Bill Brown from Evansville, Indiana; whether he is our Bill Brown is for the editor.

why: A studio portrait in a professionally printed class composite with her own nameplate beneath it. 142 by 232 pixels cut at native resolution from a 2088 by 1655 plate; not enlarged. Small, but it is a lit studio frame rather than a crop out of a crowd, and nothing else in the digitised record shows her.
how_identified: WKU Archives UA61/1, WKU Nursing Class 2000, TopSCHOLAR dlsc_ua_records/2536. The plate is a professionally printed composite of thirty-five oval studio portraits arranged round the lettering 'Western Kentucky University / Department of Nursing / Bachelor of Science / 2000', each oval with its own printed nameplate directly below it. Hers is the third portrait of the top row and the nameplate reads Leigh Bakken. The plate runs in strict alphabetical order by surname, so the third place is fixed between Samantha Bailey in the second and Teia Burchett in the fourth. One name, one face.
identification: FACE PROVED, PERSON NOT PROVED - FOR THE EDITOR
identification_reasoning: THE FACE IS PROVED: the nameplate is printed under her own oval and the alphabetical run confirms the position independently. THE PERSON IS NOT PROVED by a caption tying the nursing student to the SGA seat. WHAT ARGUES FOR IT. FIRST, the year is right to the term: this is a BACHELOR of Science class, printed on the plate itself, so its members entered the programme around 1996, and the archive's Leigh Bakken was elected to an At-Large seat in SGA Congress on 8 October 1996 after attending as a repeat visitor. SECOND, Bakken is a one-hit surname in the university's digitised record: searched all 11,850 items of the full TopSCHOLAR index and the only occurrence anywhere is this composite. THIRD, the given name matches exactly, and the archive's own note records the fuller form 'Leigh A. Bakken' from the minutes. WHAT ARGUES AGAINST IT: no source states her major, and the archive separately records a LUKE Bakken in the same Congress, named apart from her as a second absentee in the roll call of 23 November 1996. Luke is not on this plate and is not this person, but his existence shows there was more than one Bakken on the Hill in these years, so the rarity argument is weaker here than it looks. There is no Leigh Bakken anywhere else in the digitised record to check against.
